headline: 2 Bangladeshis killed as Houthi attack hits Riyadh airport
summary: At least 12 people died and over 300 were injured in the explosion. Five flights from Dhaka to Riyadh were cancelled due to the airport closure.
details: Two Bangladeshis are among the 12 people killed and 309 injured following a Houthi attack on King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia.
The attack led to the immediate closure of the airport, causing widespread disruption to air travel and flights being diverted or cancelled.
According to the Civil Aviation Authority of Bangladesh (CAAB), five flights from Dhaka to Riyadh were cancelled up until Sunday morning, including one Biman Bangladesh Airlines flight.
Biman Bangladesh Airlines suspended its BG 339 and BG 340 flights on the Dhaka-Riyadh-Dhaka route, advising passengers not to travel to the airport.
Other affected flights included several Saudia Airlines flights (SV 804, SV 805, SV 806, SV 807) and RX 763 and RX 764.
A US-Bangla Airlines flight (BS 381) was forced to divert and land elsewhere, arriving in Dhaka 12 hours later than scheduled.
Bangladesh has strongly condemned the attack on the Riyadh airport, as the same as reported by the Dhaka Tribune.
Airport authorities have advised passengers to contact their respective airlines for the latest flight status and updated schedules.
caption:
2 Bangladeshis dead and 12 killed in total as a Houthi attack hits Riyadh airport, causing massive flight cancellations from Dhaka.

Two Bangladeshis are among the 12 people killed and 309 injured following a Houthi attack on King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia.

The attack led to the immediate closure of the airport, causing widespread disruption to air travel and flights being diverted or cancelled.

According to the Civil Aviation Authority of Bangladesh (CAAB), five flights from Dhaka to Riyadh were cancelled up until Sunday morning, including one Biman Bangladesh Airlines flight.

Biman Bangladesh Airlines suspended its BG 339 and BG 340 flights on the Dhaka-Riyadh-Dhaka route, advising passengers not to travel to the airport.

Other affected flights included several Saudia Airlines flights (SV 804, SV 805, SV 806, SV 807) and RX 763 and RX 764.

A US-Bangla Airlines flight (BS 381) was forced to divert and land elsewhere, arriving in Dhaka 12 hours later than scheduled.

Bangladesh has strongly condemned the attack on the Riyadh airport, as the same as reported by the Dhaka Tribune.

Airport authorities have advised passengers to contact their respective airlines for the latest flight status and updated schedules.

headline: Air quality alert: Dhaka ranks 6th most polluted city globally
summary: The capital city faces severe air pollution levels, continuing its trend of being among the worst in the world.
details: Dhaka has been ranked as the 6th most polluted city in the world, according to recent air quality data.
The city's air quality index (AQI) frequently reaches hazardous levels, posing significant health risks to millions of residents.
Major contributors to the pollution include construction dust, vehicle emissions, and industrial smoke.
Health experts warn that prolonged exposure to these pollutants can lead to respiratory illnesses and other long-term health complications.
caption:
Dhaka is now the 6th most polluted city in the world. How bad is the air we breathe?

Dhaka has been ranked as the 6th most polluted city in the world, according to recent air quality data.

The city's air quality index (AQI) frequently reaches hazardous levels, posing significant health risks to millions of residents.

Major contributors to the pollution include construction dust, vehicle emissions, and industrial smoke.

Health experts warn that prolonged exposure to these pollutants can lead to respiratory illnesses and other long-term health complications.
